# Magic reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_magic_docs.py — do not edit by hand. -->

Magics are commands that start with `%` (line magics) or `%%` (cell magics, on the first line of a cell).
With automagic on (the default), line magics also work without the `%` when the name isn't a Python variable.
Inside ember, `%help name` shows the same details.

## General

### `%aimport`

Mark modules for autoreload 1 (%aimport -mod excludes).

### `%autoawait`

Top-level await runner: asyncio · trio · curio · off.

### `%automagic`

Toggle calling magics without the % prefix.

### `%autoreload`

Reload changed modules: 0 off · 1 %aimport-ed only · 2 all · now.

### `%clear`, `%cls`

Clear the screen.

### `%config`

Show or change settings: %config · %config name · %config name=value.

### `%copy`

Copy the last result (or an expression) to the clipboard.

### `%debug`

Post-mortem debugger on the last error, or %debug statement.

### `%doctest_mode`

Toggle plain >>> prompts and output, for copying into doctests.

### `%editmode`, `%vi`, `%emacs`

Switch key bindings: %editmode vi|emacs (or just %vi / %emacs).

### `%exit`, `%quit`

Leave ember.

### `%help`

Show keys, syntax and magics · %help name for one magic.

### `%load_ext`

Load an extension module (IPython extensions work too).

### `%lsmagic`

List all magics.

### `%pdb`

Toggle automatic post-mortem debugging on errors.

### `%profile`

Show the active profile and its directories.

### `%reload_ext`

Reload an extension.

### `%tb`

Print the last traceback again.

### `%theme`

List or switch color themes.

### `%unload_ext`

Unload an extension.

### `%xmode`

Traceback style: minimal · plain · context · verbose (no arg cycles).

## Namespace & inspection

### `%page`

Show an object's pretty repr in a pager (-r for plain repr).

### `%pdef`

Show a callable's signature.

### `%pdoc`

Show an object's docstring.

### `%pfile`

Show the whole file an object is defined in.

### `%pinfo`

Inspect an object (same as obj?).

### `%pinfo2`

Inspect an object with source (same as obj??).

### `%precision`

Float display precision: %precision 3 · %precision %.2e · %precision (reset).

### `%psearch`

Find names by wildcard: %psearch os.*path* [type] [-i] [-a].

### `%psource`

Show an object's source code.

### `%reset`

Clear variables: %reset · %reset in|out|dhist (-f accepted).

### `%reset_selective`

Delete variables whose names match a regex.

### `%who`

List user variables, optionally by type (%who int str).

### `%who_ls`

Return a sorted list of user variable names (optionally by type).

### `%whos`, `%vars`

Table of user variables with types and values.

### `%xdel`

Delete a variable and every reference ember holds to it (Out, _, _N).

## Running & timing

### `%%capture`

Capture stdout/stderr/displays: %%capture [var] [--no-stdout] [--no-stderr] [--no-display].

### `%cpaste`

Paste a block, end with a line containing only -- (or ctrl+d); prompts are stripped.

### `%paste`

Run code from the clipboard (prompts stripped): -q quiet · -r rerun last paste.

### `%prun`

Profile a statement (-s sort -l limit -r return stats -q -D dumpfile -T textfile).

### `%%prun`

Profile the cell body.

### `%run`

Run a python file or module (-i -n -e -t -d -p -m; see %help run).

```text
%run [options] file.py [args…]
  -i       run in the shell's namespace (default: fresh namespace, merged back afterwards)
  -n       don't set __name__ to "__main__"
  -e       ignore sys.exit() calls
  -t       print timing (-N count repeats it)
  -d       run under the debugger (-b file:line sets a breakpoint)
  -p       profile with cProfile (accepts %prun's -s/-l/-D/-T options)
  -m mod   run a module like `python -m`
```

### `%time`

Time a single statement or expression.

### `%%time`

Time the whole cell.

### `%timeit`

Benchmark a statement (-n loops -r runs -p precision -q quiet -o return result).

### `%%timeit`

Benchmark the cell body; the first-line text is setup code.

## History & session

### `%edit`, `%ed`

Edit a file, history range, macro or object's source in $EDITOR, then load it.

### `%history`, `%hist`

Show history: ranges like 4-6 ~1/, -g pattern, -l N, -o, -p, -n, -u, -f file.

```text
%history [options] [ranges…]
  ranges   4 · 4-6 · 4:6 (end exclusive) · ~1/ (whole previous session) · ~2/3-5
  -g [pat] search every session (glob, e.g. -g "import*")
  -l [N]   last N lines across sessions (default 10)
  -n       show line numbers   -o  include outputs   -p  add >>> prompts
  -t       show translated (python) source instead of raw input
  -u       unique lines only (with -g)
  -f file  write to a file instead of the screen
```

### `%load`

Load code into the prompt: file, url, history range or macro (-r lines, -s symbols).

### `%logon`, `%logoff`

Resume / pause logging.

### `%logstart`

Log this session's input to a file: %logstart [-o] [-r] [-t] [file [append|over|backup|rotate|global]].

### `%logstate`

Show logging status.

### `%logstop`

Stop logging and close the log file.

### `%macro`

Define a macro from history: %macro name 3-5 8 (typing the name runs it).

### `%recall`, `%rep`

Put previous input (or a range) into the prompt for editing.

### `%rerun`

Run previous input again: %rerun · %rerun 3-5 · -l N last N · -g pattern.

### `%save`

Save input to a file: %save file [ranges] (-a append, -r raw).

### `%store`

Persist variables across sessions: %store x · -r restore · -d x delete · -z clear · x >file.

```text
%store              list stored variables
%store x y          store variables (pickled)
%store -r [x …]     restore all, or some, into the namespace
%store -d x         forget a stored variable
%store -z           forget everything
%store x >file.txt  write str(x) to a file (>> appends)
```

## Shell & files

### `%alias`

Define a shell alias: %alias name command (%s = positional arg, %l = whole line).

### `%%bash`

Run the cell with bash.

### `%bookmark`

Bookmark directories: %bookmark name [dir] · -l list · -d name · -r remove all.

### `%cd`

Change directory: ~ · - · -N (from %dhist) · -b bookmark · -q quiet.

```text
%cd [-q] [dir]     go to dir (default ~); falls back to a bookmark of that name
%cd -              go back to the previous directory
%cd -N             go to entry N of %dhist
%cd -b name        go to a bookmark
```

### `%dhist`

Show visited directories: %dhist [N | from to].

### `%dirs`

Return the directory stack.

### `%env`, `%set_env`

Show env vars, or %env NAME · %env NAME=value.

### `%killbgscripts`

Terminate all background %%script processes.

### `%ls`

List a directory (-a shows hidden files).

### `%%node`

Run the cell with node.

### `%%perl`

Run the cell with perl.

### `%pip`

Run pip for this interpreter.

### `%popd`

Pop a directory off the stack and cd there.

### `%pushd`

Push the current directory on the stack and cd.

### `%pwd`

Return the working directory.

### `%%pypy`

Run the cell with pypy.

### `%%python`

Run the cell with python.

### `%%python3`

Run the cell with python3.

### `%%ruby`

Run the cell with ruby.

### `%%script`

Run the cell with any program: %%script [--bg] [--out var] [--err var] command.

### `%%sh`

Run the cell with sh.

### `%sx`, `%system`

Run a shell command and return its output lines (same as !!cmd).

### `%unalias`

Remove an alias.

### `%%writefile`

Write the cell body to a file (-a to append).

### `%%zsh`

Run the cell with zsh.

## Gui & plotting

### `%gui`

Keep a GUI event loop running at the prompt: %gui qt|tk|osx|gtk3|gtk4|wx|asyncio (no arg disables).

### `%matplotlib`

Interactive matplotlib windows that stay responsive: %matplotlib [qt|tk|osx|…] · -l list.
